summary: Friedrich Windischmann studied at Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and at Munich. Specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he served as a professor at Munich and Freising before becoming vicar general of Munich.

Friedrich Zarncke, a scholar in linguistics, studied at Rostock and Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. He spent his career at the University of Leipzig as a privatdozent and rector, and also held a post at Rostock.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, and history. After studying at the University of Leipzig, he served as director of the School of Oriental Languages in Saint Petersburg and director at the University of Vienna.

Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena, and later served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University, and held professorships at the University of Amsterdam, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Fritz Burg was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. from Humboldt University of Berlin between 1880 and 1885. He subsequently worked at the Hamburg State and University Library, serving as a librarian from 1907 to 1926.

Fritz Georg Wolff worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Munich, Berlin, Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Giessen under Christian Bartholomae.

Fritz Hommel was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Leipzig and Munich, learning under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and Friedrich Delitzsch. He spent his career on the faculty at the University of Munich from around 1877 to 1925.

Fritz Johaentgen, an Indologist, studied at the University of Bonn and the Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, earning his Ph.D. there. He subsequently served as a privatdozent at Berlin from 1864 to 1878.

Fritz Kern, a scholar of history and Indology, studied at Lausanne, Tübingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Kiel University, Goethe University Frankfurt, and the University of Bonn.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied and habilitated at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn, the University of Munich, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Frédéric Baudry, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian positions at Versailles and the Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, eventually serving as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine.

Frédéric Richard works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Lausanne and the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, later working as a coordinator at Lausanne and project manager at the Centre intercantonal d'information sur les croyances.

Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Strasbourg, Paris, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Strasbourg, teaching foreign literature and serving as professor from 1840 to 1877.

Frédéric-Gustave Eichhoff was an Indologist and linguist who received his Ph.D. from the University of Paris. He taught at the Sorbonne and served as professor of foreign literature at the University of Lyon from 1842 to 1855.
Fu Yan was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College from 1877 to 1879. He later held posts at Fudan University and Peking University.

Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a post at Academia Sinica from 1993 to 2021.
Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history who studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong. He later held an academic post at Tunghai University from around 1955 to 1969.

Fuhui Zhang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and history. She earned a Ph.D. from Northeast Normal University, where she also served as a professor in 2004, and was affiliated with Tianshui Normal University in 2012.
Fujio Oda is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kyushu University from 1952 to 1956. He later held positions at Fukuoka University from 1974 to 2004 and at Beppu University.
